findings.text: blocking: `·` (and the same use at line 30) is an HTML named entity that XML does not define, so the SVG is not well-formed and no XML-strict renderer will open it. Confirmed here: `python3 -c 'xml.dom.minidom.parse(...)'` fails with 'undefined entity: line 29, column 33', and ImageMagick's librsvg delegate refuses with 'could not read or parse the SVG' -> the figure renders nowhere, including the reckon page that embeds it at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-signed-recovery-unbind.html:32. No render check for this figure appears in gate.log, although the figures rule requires the producer to render each new SVG and look at it, which is why the defect shipped.

follow-on: the FakeGraph re-implements the SOURCE_INVARIANT predicate in Python (`if stage == "exhausted" and name_id in exempt: continue`), so the exemption clause the node added to the real Cypher at imas_codex/standard_names/source_invariant.py:59-60 (and the $exempt_ids parameter wiring at :65) is never executed by these tests: a misspelled parameter or a wrong property in that clause leaves all 11 tests green. The negative control bears this out - its third mutation removes the exhausted-name clause from the predicate and reddened neither test_source_invariant_still_refuses_a_sourceless_live_name nor test_exemption_is_confined_to_its_own_exhausted_rows.

follow-on: `_load_recovery_unbind_rows` duplicates the authority header owned by `_load_signed_stale_source_rows` at imas_codex/standard_names/signed_manifest.py:1601-1645 - read bytes, JSON parse, schema check, the same self-referential signature-contract comparison, the digest-length check and the canonical-rows SHA-256 - differing only in the schema string and the id field names. The addition extends the module's adapter registry but duplicates its loader rather than extracting a shared owner, so a fix to the header contract must now be made twice.

follow-on: the postcondition selects `source.status AS source_status` but never asserts it, so the brief's requirement that the write leave the StandardNameSource node unchanged has no check behind it; a mutation that altered the source's status while removing the edge would still satisfy every postcondition assertion (bindings == 0 and name_stage == exhausted).

follow-on: the Gate section and the manifest describe the gate as covering every test file that imports signed_manifest or source_invariant, but three such files were absent from the run (tests/standard_names/test_dd_residue_release.py, tests/standard_names/test_rewire_relocation_retire.py, tests/standard_names/test_supersede_successor_scalar.py). Re-run here: 5 collected / 5 deselected / 0 selected (EXIT=5), so the omission does not change the result - every test in them is graph-marked and deselected under the default marker set, and the three files all call apply_signed_manifest, but the record overstates the gate's reach.
